articleTitle: Antennas for Satcom-on-the-Move, Review
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This article presents a survey on vehicular antennas for on-the-move satellite communication. Main technologies developed for this service are discussed. Antennas designed by different research groups and companies are considered.

articleTitle: Design of Artificial Neural Networks with a Specified Quality of Functioning
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The general approach to development of methods for determination of quality of functioning of artificial neural networks any structure and destination has been formulated. This paper demonstrates complex index of quality (accuracy) of functioning of the artificial neural networks. The index considers values of functional tolerances. The article describes properties of the complex index and its use in examples of designing of artificial neural networks. These networks were used for approximating of basic mathematical functions and estimating of amplitude of harmonic signals containing noise component. Dependence of quality of functioning of artificial neural networks on a chosen training function was shown.

articleTitle: Apriori Viterbi Model for Prior Detection of Socio-Technical Attacks in a Social Network
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Social network analysis is a basic mechanism to observe the behavior of a community in society. In the huge and complex social network formed using cyberspace or telecommunication technology, the identification or prediction of any kind of socio-technical attack is always difficult. This challenge creates an opportunity to explore different methodologies, concepts and algorithms used to identify these kinds of community on the basis of certain pattern, properties, structure and trend in their linkage. This paper tries to find the hidden information in huge social network by compressing it in small networks through apriori algorithm and then diagnosed using viterbi algorithm to predict the most probable pattern of conversation to be followed in the network and if this pattern matches with the existing pattern of criminals, terrorists and hijackers then it may be helpful to generate some kind of alert before crime.

articleTitle: Neural Networks Realizations Using Memristors
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This article overviews modern approaches to neural networks hardware realization using memristors - passive nanoscale elements, which resistance changes according to charge flow through it.

articleTitle: Development of Information Security's Theoretical Aspects in Cloud Technology with the Use of Threshold Structures
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The article explores the construction of systems information security in cloud systems and aspects of its effective using. Special attention is given to questions of the protection of the organization through the use of cloud technology secret sharing schemes (SSS) interlaced with Residue number system (RNS). It is shown that the level of protection of secret information is processed using cloud technologies using RNS depends on the threshold value used in the SSS and the size of the modules RNS. Modified neural network of a finite ring for the effective implementation of modular operations in RNS.

Author Keywords: neural network of a finite ring

articleTitle: Fast Quality Assessment of Videos Transmitted over Lossy Networks
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Analysing the ability of networking protocols to stream real-time video data over lossy networks, many researchers are faced to the problem of video quality estimation, for which the MSE and PSNR metrics are widely used. However, many existing tools used to calculate these metrics do not take into account frame losses inevitable with video streaming over wireless networks. Other tools do account for frame losses but work too slowly. The paper proposes a novel method allowing to speed up greatly video quality metric computation.

articleTitle: The First Steps of Soviet Computer Science
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The report provides new facts about the history of the first computers in the Soviet Union from 1948 to 1952. Four teams from the Academy of Sciences and Industry, almost simultaneously began work on developing of the first computers. The victory was won by the team that had the fewest resources. At the end of 1951 the first Soviet computer M1 was put into service.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of the Power Line Communication Channel
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Power line communications may be used as a data communication channel in public and indoor distribution networks so that it does not require the installing of new cables. Primarily, it is aimed at a realization of basic power line communication model for PLC communication. The different levels of mapping carrier frequencies in OFDM (QPSK, 16-QAM) were simulated on the proposed model.

articleTitle: Data Handling in GNSS Receiver Network and Ionosphere Monitoring Service Solution
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This paper describes software and hardware solution that enables Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data acquisition with ground based stations network. The solution relies on original data format and relational database management system. C++ library code and database schema SQL-structures are created automatically from Javads Receiver External Interface Specification (GREIS) with a C# application. This solution was used to create a real time ionosphere monitor service based on Feodorov Institute of Applied Geophysics ROSHYDROMET GNSS-receiver network.

articleTitle: Searching of Unknown Earth-Orbiting Object in the Next Observation Session
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The problems of short-arc initial orbit determination and nonlinear propagation of uncertainty region are considered in the context of searching in the next observation sessions of an Earth-orbiting object with a priori unknown orbit. To solve these problems a new algorithm is proposed based on piecewise-linear approximation of nonlinearities, and piecewise-Gaussian representation of posteriori density function.

articleTitle: Toward Optimal Design of the Generalized Shiryaev -- Roberts Procedure for Quickest Change-Point Detection under Exponential Observations
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: We consider the basic quickest change-point detection problem with optimality understood in Pollak's minimax sense. The topic of interest is optimal design of the emerging Generalized Shiryaev-Roberts (GSR) detection procedure. To optimize the GSR procedure, we exploit the fact that the GSR procedure provides a lower bound on Pollak's minimax Supremum (conditional) Average Detection Delay (SADD). Specifically, we propose to optimize the GSR procedure by choosing its head start and detection threshold so as to bring the lower bound as far up as is possible within the set tolerable Average Run Length (ARL) to false alarm level. We then follow through with this idea and carry out a case study where, in a specific exponential scenario, we solve the respective lower bound-vs-ARL tradeoff numerically, and tabulate the obtained optimal head start, detection threshold, and the maximized lower bound. The study is extensive in that it considers changes of diverse magnitudes and a wide range of levels of the ARL to false alarm, the latter are computed exactly. The study aids gain further insight into the GSR procedure as well as into the still-unsolved question of what minimizes Pollak's SADD for a given level of the ARL to false alarm. Also, the tabulated optimal head start-detection-threshold pairs might help an engineer to properly set up the GSR procedure.

articleTitle: Multipath Detection of Uncertain Waveform Signals in Phased-Array Radars
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: It is well-known that the problem of radio direction finding (RDF) appears in various shortwave systems in the case of multipath signal propagation. Direction-finding algorithm development has been facilitated with the invention and widespread usage of phased-array radars. However, RDF problem has not been solved yet, because of various limitations imposed on formulations and solutions in developed algorithms (e.g, the waveform of detected signal is assumed to be known). This article provides new recurrent algorithm with super resolution properties, based on adaptive Bayesian approach, which works in the case, when there is no any priory information about a waveform of the received signal.

articleTitle: Construction of Automatic Control System above Ground Transport by H-Bahn Technology: Concept, Initial Data and Statement Objectives
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The article describes the project of construction of automatic control system above ground transport by H-Bahn technology within State contract. It shows the advantages and distinctive characteristics of above ground trains. It presents a list of works and results developed within the project. It describes the work performed in accordance with specification and schedule of works.

articleTitle: Multi-h CPM Signal Format Selection for Communication Systems with Complex Jamming Environment
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This article considers signal formats of multi-h CPM which are created with use of a rectangular frequency pulse, a frequency pulse in the form of a sine wave half-cycle and in the form of a raised cosine of various lengths. The authors provide combined data on the error probability for receiving of the best multi-h CPM formats in the environment with flat and non-fluctutional noises. The multi-h CPM signals with a good noise resistance in the flat noise environment remain energy-effective in a more complex jamming environment. One of the important parameters of CPM signals is their spectral efficiency characterized by the degree of band limitedness and spectrum rectangularity. The article provides the best signal formats which were selected after all of the received noise resistance characteristics and spectral indices were compared.

articleTitle: Regularized Image Reconstruction from Projections Method
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: We propose a new image reconstruction from projection method consistent with the maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) approach, i.e. using regularization. We compare reconstruction with three regularization methods -- Tikhonov regularization, smoothed total variation regularization, and early stopping. We compute a number of objective evaluation measures and compare the reconstruction results. We conclude that the best result, both in terms of subjective and objective assessment, is obtained for smoothed total variation regularization.

articleTitle: Iterative Algorithm for Solving of Linear Algebraic Equations Systems without Multi-bit Multiplication Operation
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: An iterative method of the systems of the linear algebraic equations solution, excluding the multi-bit multiplication operation while designing the special-purpose computing facilities is considered. Algorithmization of the iteration process is based on the use of the first order delta-transformations with the variable quantum that can significantly reduce the number of iterations in comparison with the using of the constant quantum. The optimal estimations characterizing the duration of idealized iterative loops with constant quantum of a certain value are formed. In theoretical justification quasi-optimal conditions determining a way of the representation a sequence of variable quanta values in the loops and based on using two or four idealized iterations within each loop are developed for the purpose of the real processes. Besides the quanta values shall be represented in the form of a shift operation? that allows realizing the implementation of the iterative process without using the multiplication of the multi-bit codes. There are also effective ways to complete the iteration in each loop. The findings of investigation of the iterative solution of various systems of the linear algebraic equations different with convergence rate are given in the work. The possibility of reduction the number of iterations in comparison with the using the delta-transformations with the constant quantum to hundreds -- thousands of times is shown when ensuring the identical accuracy. The number of iterations with variable quantum is to a considerable extent approximate the number of iterations to the simple iteration method.

Author Keywords: systems of the linear algebraic equations

articleTitle: Importance of Seismic Data Resolution on Geological Results of Multidisciplinary Geophysical Research including 3D Geological Modeling
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This paper overviews actual problem regarding importance of seismic data resolution on geological results and multidisciplinary geophysical research. The results presented in the paper illustrate the different case studies carried out in Poland for conventional and unconventional reservoir aimed at comparison of the methodology applied to different geological settings and formation character.

articleTitle: Bounds of Cardinality on Subspace Network Codes
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Network coding is a new direction in the information and communication theory. In this area algebraic coding for wire channels is based on Grassmann metric which is also called subspace metric. In the theory the main problem is to construct codes with great cardinality and create fast decoding algorithms. Here, we deliver the low bound of subspace network codes. We calculate cardinality of some concrete codes and describe decoding algorithms. We show the interest cases where the cardinality approaches the upper bound.

articleTitle: FIR Filters in Two-Stage Residue Number System
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to the implementation of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters in the Residue Number System (RNS). The essence of the method is to use the two-stage RNS, wherein uses two RNS: first RNS for transforming the input signal, and the second RNS for transforming of computational channels of the first RNS. This approach significantly reduces bit width of data, however, it requires to perform additional operations of forward and reverse conversion. Nevertheless modeling of FIR filters using the proposed architecture showed reducing the processing time in comparison with the known analogues.

articleTitle: Modern Software Tools for New Computing Architectures Development
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Microprocessor architecture development is a long and complicated process. The use of modern advanced software tools helps to accelerate the development process and increases the efficiency of the produced processor. This paper presents basic software tools and their quality improvements. Tool chain development is performed in parallel with the development of the architecture. There are open source solutions, such as the GNU Compiler Collection or LLVM, enabling the rapid prototyping of a compiler for the new architecture. But for the effective use of the architectural features more complex tools like Universal Translating Library are used. This library contains advanced algorithms for analysis and optimization, as well as a mechanism for their integration with any technological chain like GNU or LLVM. Before development of microprocessor design is completed functional simulator is used for testing and debugging of other software components like operating system or applications. Simulator plays the role of the reference model of the microprocessor. The simulator execution time is critical for development so most heavy parts should be optimized. In this paper it is proposed a flag computation method which is two times faster than the popular method of table based flags computation. In the segment of embedded operating systems compact real-time OS are widely used. These OS are linked with the user applications. They do not support multitasking, but support multithreading. One example of such OS is a specialized real-time operating system Milandr OS. Milandr OS was designed to control the operation of integrated modules. Language PPDL is designed for rapid prototyping and verification of new architectures, as well as creation of system software. Its basic principle: single description - several components. From a unified description of core microprocessor or coprocessor its Verilog-description and a number of software components can be generated: QEMU based simulator, assembler/disassembler, the interface to connect to the debugger, and a set of tests. The most important stage in the development of the microprocessor is verification process. Automatic test generators are used to solve this problem. Automatically generated tests allow debugging of functional simulator and then debugging of RTL-architecture description. Integration of verification system and PPDL results in significant reduction of routine verification work. One approach to launch of a new microprocessor on the market is a binary compatibility with existing solutions by using dynamic translation. Besides compatibility dynamic translation solves the issues of improving performance by optimizing JIT-compiler. Elbrus microprocessor is an example of x86 compatible system.

articleTitle: Technologies and Theory for Multilevel Ecological Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Technology and mathematics for monitoring systems construction and optimization are presented. Different approaches to the hypotheses testing (as theoretical basis of objects detection) are compared. For monitoring of artificial objects mathematical model of nondestructive testing was developed. Proposed prove of monitoring economical efficiency may be used by projections of big monitoring systems, including global ones.

Author Keywords: errors of the 1-st and the 2-nd kinds

articleTitle: Metrological Support of the Antenna Measurements in JSC "Radiofizika" Overview
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: An overview of metrological support of antenna measurements in JSC 'Radiofizika' is given. The items of antenna measurements, EMC measurements, radar systems adjustment and testing are considered. The advantages of using the anechoic chamber to provide precise testing for large spectrum of antenna systems are demonstrated. This overview is devoted to the 80-th anniversary of Georgy G. Bubnov - founding father and first director of the company.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Optimal Heat Detector Deployment for Fire Detection
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), composed of spatially distributed autonomous sensor nodes, have a wide range of application. One of the most interesting phenomena that can be monitored by WSN, among various physical, chemical and biological phenomena and different kind of events, is fire. In case of fire presence continuous monitoring and/or recording of sensitive or restricted parts are necessary for timely response and reaction. Fire monitoring applications require accurate deployment of the sensor nodes because their positions have a dramatic impact on the effectiveness of the WSN and the efficiency of its operation. The choice of the deployment scheme depends highly on the type of sensors, application and the environment that the sensors will operate in (residential buildings, hospitals, historical buildings, malls etc.). The main advantage of WSN usage can be also identified as a simple reconfiguration and maintenance of the created infrastructure, what can be of great importance for systems that are physically unaffected by changes, but they tend to change in terms of safety (e.g. ships, oil productive platforms, etc.). Knowing that the positions of nodes have a dramatic impact on the effectiveness of the WSN and the efficiency of its operation, in this paper the various strategies for positioning nodes in WSNs are considered: grid, triangular and strip. The objective of this paper is to properly place the heat detectors in certain indoor area, in such way that next two important network design objectives are satisfied: to maximize the network lifetime after fire ignition and to use a minimum number of sensors in order to achieve full area coverage.

articleTitle: Basis Functions of the Multidimensional CMAC Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The short introduction to the cerebellar model articulation controller (the CMAC neural network) and its main properties are presented. It is shown that the basis functions of the CMAC neural network are given implicitly, the number of these function is finite, and they have the incorrect pyramid forms. The expressions for the number of these function is given.

articleTitle: Microseismic Sounding Technology Development for Engineering Applications
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Description of the Micro seismic Sounding Technology developed by the authors for the investigation of the Earth crust deep structure (including oil & gas deposits) is presented. Developing technology allows effectively allocate the velocity in homogeneities and has significant informative and economic advantages under deep depth investigation in comparison with known seismic methods. The basic idea of the developed approach is the following: geological heterogeneity (for example, mineral deposits or underground reservoirs filled with oil, gas or fresh water), manifest themselves like the micro seismic wave field anomalies at the Earth's surface. Developed technology is based on the allocation of anomalies in deep micro seismic wave field spectrum in the area of the probable geological heterogeneity (mineral deposits).

articleTitle: Automatic Control of Ballistic Missiles Characteristics Using Mobile Radar Data at Prior Parametric Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: Let us analyze the methods of ballistic missiles throw-mass estimation based on radar observations of different BM trajectory phases from the moment of launching to the moment of detachable elements drop. It is necessary to give approximate accuracy estimations of the resulting mass evaluations under the condition of information obtainment by modern radars from three main phase of the BM trajectory. Based on the statistical-decision theory methods, it is necessary to obtain the analytical expressions for true automatic control of BM parameters in prior uncertainty conditions versus the nuisance parameters. It is assumed that the nuisance parameters are related to the controlled parameters through some arbitrary functional dependences, and the nuisance parameters are estimated by the learning measurements sample. The general expression for validity shall be specified for two types of control tasks: by the mean vector and jointly by the mean vector and by the correlation controlled parameters matrix.

articleTitle: A Digital Network Manufacturing System -- Materialization of Ideas
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The Digital Network Manufacturing System concept assumes the integration of tools and approaches from Product Lifecycle Management, advanced manufacturing technologies, Systems Analysis and Engineering, Model-Based Engineering, and other engineering/management areas related to the development, introduction, production, and support of innovative products. This paper outlines the major features of the concept and the tool-kits that have been developed in engineering, computer science, telecommunications, technology and some other disciplines that enable its realization. The concept is based upon experience gained from the development of new products and technologies in the U.S. aerospace sector.

articleTitle: Novel Dilute III-nitride Materials Growth and Characterization for Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2014 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication
abstract: The conventional group III-nitrides (AlN, GaN and InN) and their alloys represent an important class of direct band gap semiconductors. These materials have exhibited exceptional physical properties and high potentials for their use in numerous commercial applications beyond the capabilities of silicon technology. The direct wide band gaps, intrinsic high carrier mobility and the abilities to form heterostructures have allowed these materials to dominate in the photonic and electronic device market (e.g., light emitters, photodiodes and high-speed/high power electronics). In this paper we have presented an overview of the structural, electrical, phonon and optical properties of III-nitrides with special emphasis on characterizing their lattice dynamical and defect traits. Discussions on the benefits of binary and ternary alloys are focused in the context of using them to prepare quantum wells and super lattice structures in designing devices from ultraviolet photo-conductors, visible light-emitting-diodes and laser diodes. After summarizing the current status of conventional materials, we have evaluate their dynamical and defect properties with implications of exploiting these and other non-conventional III-nitrides for future applications.
